L24: # OpenProcess function (processthreadsapi.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: Opens an existing local process object.
L33: 
L34: ## Syntax
L35: 
L36:     `HANDLE OpenProcess(
L37:       [in] DWORD dwDesiredAccess,
L38:       [in] BOOL  bInheritHandle,
L39:       [in] DWORD dwProcessId
L40:     );
L41:     `
L42: ## Parameters
L43: 
L44: `[in] dwDesiredAccess`
L45: 
L46: The access to the process object. This access right is checked against the security descriptor for the process. This parameter can be one or more of the 【5†process access rights】.
L47: 
L48: If the caller has enabled the 【6†SeDebugPrivilege privilege】, the requested access is granted regardless of the contents of the security descriptor.
L49: 
L50: `[in] bInheritHandle`
L51: If this value is TRUE, processes created by this process will inherit the handle. Otherwise, the processes do not inherit this handle.
L52: 
L53: `[in] dwProcessId`
L54: 
L55: The identifier of the local process to be opened.
L56: If the specified process is the System Idle Process (0x00000000), the function fails and the last error code is `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. If the specified process is the System process or one of the Client Server Run-Time Subsystem (CSRSS) processes, this function fails and the last error code is `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` because their access restrictions prevent user-level code from opening them.
L57: If you are using 【7†GetCurrentProcessId】 as an argument to this function, consider using 【8†GetCurrentProcess】 instead of OpenProcess, for improved performance.
L58: ## Return value
L59: 
L60: If the function succeeds, the return value is an open handle to the specified process.
L61: 
L62: If the function fails, the return value is NULL. To get extended error information, call 【9†GetLastError】.
L63: ## Remarks
L64: 
L65: To open a handle to another local process and obtain full access rights, you must enable the SeDebugPrivilege privilege. For more information, see 【10†Changing Privileges in a Token】.
L66: 
L67: The handle returned by the OpenProcess function can be used in any function that requires a handle to a process, such as the 【11†wait functions】, provided the appropriate access rights were requested.
L68: 
L69: When you are finished with the handle, be sure to close it using the 【12†CloseHandle】 function.
L70: #### Examples
L71: 
L72: For an example, see 【13†Taking a Snapshot and Viewing Processes】.
L73:

L24: # GetTokenInformation function (securitybaseapi.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The GetTokenInformation function retrieves a specified type of information about an 【5†access token】. The calling process must have appropriate access rights to obtain the information.
L33: 
L34: To determine if a user is a member of a specific group, use the 【6†CheckTokenMembership】 function. To determine group membership for app container tokens, use the 【7†CheckTokenMembershipEx】 function.
L35: ## Syntax
L36: 
L37:     `BOOL GetTokenInformation(
L38:       [in]            HANDLE                  TokenHandle,
L39:       [in]            TOKEN_INFORMATION_CLASS TokenInformationClass,
L40:       [out, optional] LPVOID                  TokenInformation,
L41:       [in]            DWORD                   TokenInformationLength,
L42:       [out]           PDWORD                  ReturnLength
L43:     );
L44:     `
L45: ## Parameters
L46: 
L47: `[in] TokenHandle`
L48: 
L49: A handle to an access token from which information is retrieved. If TokenInformationClass specifies TokenSource, the handle must have TOKEN_QUERY_SOURCE access. For all other TokenInformationClass values, the handle must have TOKEN_QUERY access.
L50: 
L51: `[in] TokenInformationClass`
L52: Specifies a value from the 【8†TOKEN_INFORMATION_CLASS】 enumerated type to identify the type of information the function retrieves. Any callers who check the TokenIsAppContainer and have it return 0 should also verify that the caller token is not an identify level impersonation token. If the current token is not an app container but is an identity level token, you should return AccessDenied.
L53: 
L54: `[out, optional] TokenInformation`
L55: A pointer to a buffer the function fills with the requested information. The structure put into this buffer depends upon the type of information specified by the TokenInformationClass parameter.
L56: 
L57: `[in] TokenInformationLength`
L58: 
L59: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by the TokenInformation parameter. If TokenInformation is NULL, this parameter must be zero.
L60: 
L61: `[out] ReturnLength`
L62: A pointer to a variable that receives the number of bytes needed for the buffer pointed to by the TokenInformation parameter. If this value is larger than the value specified in the TokenInformationLength parameter, the function fails and stores no data in the buffer.
L63: If the value of the TokenInformationClass parameter is TokenDefaultDacl and the token has no default DACL, the function sets the variable pointed to by ReturnLength to `sizeof(`【9†TOKEN_DEFAULT_DACL】`)` and sets the DefaultDacl member of the TOKEN_DEFAULT_DACL structure to NULL.
L64: ## Return value
L65: 
L66: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero.
L67: 
L68: If the function fails, the return value is zero. To get extended error information, call 【10†GetLastError】.
L69:
